seo.description: 20 High-yield JEE Main MCQ practice questions covering 2D relative motion, shortest path (zero drift), minimum crossing time, rain-man umbrella tilt angle, and 2D collision vector conditions.
seo.keywords: JEE Main Physics, Kinematics DPP, Relative Velocity in 2D, River Boat Problems, Rain Man Umbrella Angle, Minimum Drift, Shortest Path Crossing, Syed Mazhar Ali, SMA Physics

conceptCapsule.title: Vector Formulation of Two-Dimensional Relative Velocity
conceptCapsule.summary: For 2D relative kinematics: $\vec{v}_{A/B} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B$. In river-boat problems, $\vec{v}_{b} = \vec{v}_{b/r} + \vec{v}_r$. (1) For shortest time, steer normal to the flow ($\theta = 0^\circ$, $T_{\min} = \frac{d}{v}$, drift $x = \frac{ud}{v}$). (2) For shortest path / zero drift ($v > u$), steer upstream at $\sin\theta = \frac{u}{v}$ ($T = \frac{d}{\sqrt{v^2-u^2}}$). (3) If $u > v$, minimum drift is $x_{\min} = d\sqrt{\frac{u^2}{v^2}-1}$ when $\sin\theta = \frac{v}{u}$. In rain-man kinematics, umbrella must be held aligned with $\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m$.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: When drawing the umbrella angle, always determine the vector $\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m$. The rain appears to strike along $\vec{v}_{r/m}$, so the umbrella must be held pointing in the opposite direction ($-\vec{v}_{r/m}$). For two particles in 2D with positions $\vec{r}_1, \vec{r}_2$ and constant velocities $\vec{v}_1, \vec{v}_2$, the collision condition is that the relative position vector must be antiparallel to the relative velocity vector.

questions.statement: A river of width $d$ flows with speed $u$. A swimmer can swim with speed $v$ ($v > u$) in still water. The time taken to cross the river along the shortest path (zero drift) is:
questions.solution:
1. For zero drift, the swimmer heads upstream at angle $\theta$ to the normal such that $v\sin\theta = u \implies \sin\theta = u/v$.
2. Net velocity across river: $v_y = v\cos\theta = \sqrt{v^2 - u^2}$.
3. Time taken: $t = \frac{d}{\sqrt{v^2 - u^2}}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Rain is falling vertically downwards with speed $30\text{ m/s}$. A man cycles due east at $10\text{ m/s}$. The angle with the vertical at which he should hold his umbrella to protect himself from the rain is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{v}_r = -30\hat{j}$, $\vec{v}_m = 10\hat{i}$.
2. $\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m = -10\hat{i} - 30\hat{j}$.
3. The umbrella must point along $+10\hat{i} + 30\hat{j}$ (tilted towards East).
4. $\tan\theta = \frac{10}{30} = \frac{1}{3} \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\text{ towards east}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A boat crosses a river of width $1\text{ km}$ flowing at $3\text{ km/h}$. The boat is steered perpendicular to the flow with speed $4\text{ km/h}$ relative to water. The net drift of the boat on reaching the opposite bank is:
questions.solution:
1. Crossing time: $t = \frac{d}{v_{b/r}} = \frac{1\text{ km}}{4\text{ km/h}} = 0.25\text{ h}$.
2. Drift along river flow: $x = u \times t = 3\text{ km/h} \times 0.25\text{ h} = 0.75\text{ km}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: To cross a river in the shortest possible time, a swimmer should steer:

options.text: Exactly perpendicular to the direction of river flow

questions.solution:
Crossing time is $t = \frac{d}{v\cos\theta}$. To minimize $t$, $\cos\theta$ must be maximum ($\cos\theta = 1 \implies \theta = 0^\circ$). The swimmer must head perpendicular to the river flow.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Rain appears to fall vertically to a man walking at $4\text{ km/h}$. When he doubles his speed to $8\text{ km/h}$ in the same direction, rain appears to fall at $45^\circ$ to the vertical. The true velocity of rain has magnitude:
questions.solution:
1. Let $\vec{v}_r = v_x\hat{i} - v_y\hat{j}$.
2. At $v_m = 4$: $\vec{v}_{r/m} = (v_x - 4)\hat{i} - v_y\hat{j}$. Vertical $\implies v_x = 4\text{ km/h}$.
3. At $v_m = 8$: $\vec{v}_{r/m} = (4 - 8)\hat{i} - v_y\hat{j} = -4\hat{i} - v_y\hat{j}$.
4. $\tan(45^\circ) = \frac{4}{v_y} = 1 \implies v_y = 4\text{ km/h}$.
5. True speed: $v_r = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2} = 4\sqrt{2}\text{ km/h}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A river is flowing with velocity $v_r = 5\text{ km/h}$. A boat has speed $v_{b/r} = 3\text{ km/h}$ ($v_{b/r} < v_r$). The minimum drift possible for the boat while crossing the river of width $d = 400\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. When $v_{b/r} < v_r$, minimum drift angle satisfies $\sin\theta = \frac{v_{b/r}}{v_r} = \frac{3}{5}$.
2. $\cos\theta = 4/5$, $v_x = 5 - 3(3/5) = 16/5\text{ km/h}$, $v_y = 3(4/5) = 12/5\text{ km/h}$.
3. $x_{\min} = d\left(\frac{v_x}{v_y}\right) = 400 \times \frac{4}{3} \approx 533.3\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A man standing on a road has to hold his umbrella at $30^\circ$ with the vertical to keep rain away. He throws away the umbrella and starts running at $10\text{ km/h}$ in the horizontal direction. He finds that rain drops now hit his head vertically. The actual speed of the rain drops with respect to ground is:
questions.solution:
1. At rest: $\tan(30^\circ) = \frac{v_x}{v_y} \implies v_x = \frac{v_y}{\sqrt{3}}$.
2. Running at $10\text{ km/h}$, relative horizontal velocity is zero $\implies v_x = 10\text{ km/h} \implies v_y = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ km/h}$.
3. Actual speed: $v_r = \sqrt{10^2 + (10\sqrt{3})^2} = 20\text{ km/h}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A swimmer wishes to reach a point directly opposite on the other bank of a river flowing at $2\text{ m/s}$. His swimming speed in still water is $4\text{ m/s}$. At what angle to the direction of river flow must he direct his strokes?
questions.solution:
1. Upstream angle with normal: $\sin\theta = \frac{u}{v} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = 30^\circ$.
2. Angle with downstream river flow: $\alpha = 90^\circ + 30^\circ = 120^\circ$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A boat moves relative to water with velocity $v$ and river flow velocity is $u$. If the time taken by the boat to travel a distance $x$ downstream and back upstream is $T_1$, and the time taken to travel the same distance $x$ across the river and back along the shortest path is $T_2$, the ratio $T_1 / T_2$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $T_1 = \frac{x}{v+u} + \frac{x}{v-u} = \frac{2vx}{v^2 - u^2}$.
2. $T_2 = \frac{2x}{\sqrt{v^2 - u^2}}$.
3. Ratio: $\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{v}{\sqrt{v^2 - u^2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^2/v^2}}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Rain is falling with a speed of $12\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ with the vertical towards east. A cyclist rides towards east. If the rain appears to fall vertically to the cyclist, the speed of the cyclist is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{v}_r = (12\sqrt{3}\sin 30^\circ)\hat{i} - (12\sqrt{3}\cos 30^\circ)\hat{j} = 6\sqrt{3}\hat{i} - 18\hat{j}$.
2. For relative velocity to be vertical, horizontal component must be zero: $6\sqrt{3} - v_c = 0 \implies v_c = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A swimmer crosses a river flowing with speed $u$. In crossing in minimum time $T_{\min}$, he incurs a drift $x_1$. In crossing with minimum drift, the time taken is $T$. If $v > u$, the drift $x_1$ equals:
questions.solution:
1. Minimum time corresponds to heading directly across: $T_{\min} = \frac{d}{v}$.
2. Downstream drift $x_1 = u \times T_{\min} = \frac{ud}{v}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A man moves due north at $3\text{ km/h}$. Rain appears to fall vertically with speed $4\text{ km/h}$. The actual speed and direction of the rain with respect to ground are:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{v}_m = 3\hat{j}$, $\vec{v}_{r/m} = -4\hat{k} \implies \vec{v}_r = 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$.
2. Actual speed $= \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\text{ km/h}$.
3. Angle with vertical $= \tan^{-1}(3/4)$ south of vertical.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Ship $A$ is travelling due east at $10\text{ km/h}$ and ship $B$ is travelling due north at $10\text{ km/h}$. The velocity of ship $A$ relative to ship $B$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{v}_A = 10\hat{i}$, $\vec{v}_B = 10\hat{j}$.
2. $\vec{v}_{A/B} = 10\hat{i} - 10\hat{j}$.
3. Magnitude $= 10\sqrt{2}\text{ km/h}$, directed towards South-East.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A boat which has a speed of $5\text{ km/h}$ in still water crosses a river of width $1\text{ km}$ along the shortest possible path in $15\text{ minutes}$. The velocity of the river water is:
questions.solution:
1. Shortest path $\implies v_y = \sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2}$.
2. $v_y = \frac{1\text{ km}}{0.25\text{ h}} = 4\text{ km/h}$.
3. $4 = \sqrt{5^2 - v_r^2} \implies 16 = 25 - v_r^2 \implies v_r = 3\text{ km/h}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: For a person moving with velocity $\vec{v}_m$ in rain of velocity $\vec{v}_r$, the apparent velocity $\vec{v}_{r/m}$ is:
questions.solution:
By the standard definition of relative velocity: $$\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A person standing on an open truck moving horizontally with constant speed $v$ experiences rain falling at angle $	heta$ with the vertical. When the truck accelerates forward, the angle $	heta$ with the vertical will:
questions.solution:
$\tan\theta = \frac{v_{\text{truck}}}{v_{\text{rain}}}$. As the truck accelerates, $v_{\text{truck}}$ increases, hence $\tan\theta$ increases, meaning $\theta$ increases.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two particles $A$ and $B$ move with constant velocities $\vec{v}_1$ and $\vec{v}_2$. At initial moment $t = 0$, their position vectors are $\vec{r}_1$ and $\vec{r}_2$. The condition for collision of $A$ and $B$ is:
questions.solution:
Collision condition: $\vec{r}_1 + \vec{v}_1 t = \vec{r}_2 + \vec{v}_2 t \implies \vec{r}_1 - \vec{r}_2 = (\vec{v}_2 - \vec{v}_1)t$. Since $t > 0$, the unit vectors must be strictly equal: $$\frac{\vec{r}_1 - \vec{r}_2}{|\vec{r}_1 - \vec{r}_2|} = \frac{\vec{v}_2 - \vec{v}_1}{|\vec{v}_2 - \vec{v}_1|}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Raindrops are falling vertically with a velocity $10\text{ m/s}$. To a cyclist moving due north, rain appears to come at $45^\circ$ to vertical. The velocity of the cyclist is:
questions.solution:
$\tan(45^\circ) = \frac{v_c}{v_r} = 1 \implies v_c = v_r = 10\text{ m/s due north}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A boat can travel with speed $v_{b/r}$ in still water. If river flow is $v_r$ ($v_r > v_{b/r}$), to achieve minimum drift the angle $	heta$ of steering with the upstream direction must satisfy:
questions.solution:
Drift $x = \frac{d}{v_{b/r}\cos\theta}(v_r - v_{b/r}\sin\theta)$. Setting $\frac{dx}{d\theta} = 0$ yields $\sin\theta = \frac{v_{b/r}}{v_r}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A flag is mounted on a car moving due north with speed $9\text{ m/s}$. Wind blows due east with speed $12\text{ m/s}$. The direction in which the flag flutters is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{v}_{w/c} = \vec{v}_w - \vec{v}_c = 12\hat{i} - 9\hat{j}$.
2. Direction: $\tan\theta = \frac{9}{12} = \frac{3}{4}$ south of east.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
